The [flagship project 2][proj2] of the [Public Data Lab][pdl][^pdl] _"An index 
of multiple deprivation in the Canton of Zurich"_ has published a policy brief 
that is interesting, I think, for anybody working with spatial units in 
Switzerland.[^transp] Titled "[Geographische Einheiten in der Schweiz und in 
Zürich][brief]", the brief lists many (more or less commonly used) 
regionalisations and characterises them:

[![Spatial units in Switzerland and Zurich (source: Louis Moser and Ross Purves)](spatial-units.jpg "Spatial units in Switzerland and Zurich (source: Louis Moser and Ross Purves)")][brief]

I think this is an interesting resource in itself, especially if you work on 
topics were spatial units may be important for analyses and/or visualisations. 

For the PDL project team this policy brief is just a stepping stone: They aim 
to build an index of multiple deprivation ([similar to the UK][imd]). If that 
interests you, there is [a podcast episode][pod] (in Swiss-German) which covers 
that research.

[proj2]: https://publicdatalab.ch/en/leuchtturmprojekte/leuchtturmprojekt-2/
[pdl]: https://publicdatalab.ch/en/
[brief]: https://publicdatalab.ch/geographische-einheiten-in-der-schweiz-und-in-zuerich/
[pod]: https://www.dizh.uzh.ch/2026/11/19/wie-daten-mehrfachbenachteiligung-sichtbar-machen/
[imd]: https://data.geods.ac.uk/dataset/index-of-multiple-deprivation-imd

[^pdl]: The [Public Data Lab](https://spatialists.ch/posts/2025/10/26-launch-of-the-public-data-lab/) 
(PDL) is a Zurich initiative that aims to collect and analyse data, combine it 
into indicators and support informed decisions. It comprises representatives 
from the Statistical Office of the Canton of Zurich, the University of Zurich, 
the Zurich University of the Arts, and Opendata.ch.
[^transp]: Transparency note: I am a member of the Public Data Lab's advisory 
board. I do not work on the topics covered here, but had a short exchange with 
the authors.
